blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, why does `substring()` take O(n) time while `charAt()` takes O(1)?

options.text: substring() walks from index 0 to find where beginIndex is
options.says: The page says charAt reaches an index directly; the cost of substring is copying, not searching.

options.text: substring() copies its characters into a new String object
options.says: The page says substring creates a new String object, which involves copying characters.

options.text: substring() adds its new String to the String pool first
options.says: The page says nothing of the pool here; it puts the cost in copying the characters.

questions.stem: Per this page, why is `str.isEmpty()` preferred over `str.length() == 0`?

options.text: isEmpty() reads more clearly, for exactly the same work
options.says: The page prefers isEmpty() for readability and notes that the two do the same work.

options.text: isEmpty() counts a String of only spaces as empty too
options.says: Only isBlank() treats whitespace as empty; the page calls the two checks equivalent.

options.text: isEmpty() avoids the NullPointerException on null
options.says: The page says every one of these methods throws NullPointerException on a null String.

concepts: length() and charAt() take constant time, while substring() copies its characters into a new String.
isEmpty() reads better than length() == 0 and does the same work.
